meta.title: Personal mobility devices, bicycles, mopeds and convoys
meta.summary: You will learn where cyclists, e-scooter riders and moped riders may travel and under what rules, what this means for a car driver, what rights drivers with a mobility disability have, and how to travel in a convoy in poor visibility.

lesson.h: Why a driver needs to know the rules for personal mobility devices and bicycles
p: Cyclists and e-scooter riders have no bodywork to protect them. Any mistake by a driver is more dangerous for them than for another car. If you know where they are supposed to ride and what is forbidden for them, you can anticipate where they might appear from.
Chapter 24 of the Rules sets out additional requirements for e-scooters, bicycles, small electric vehicles (hoverboards, monowheels and similar devices), horse-drawn carts and the herding of animals.

lesson.h: Cyclists: where they may ride, and from what age
p: A cyclist rides on a cycle track or cycle lane. If there is none, they ride at the right-hand edge of the carriageway (including in a lane for route vehicles) in single file, or on the shoulder, the pavement or a footpath, without endangering pedestrians ⟦16⟧.

Children under 14 must not ride a bicycle at the right-hand edge of the carriageway, in a lane for route vehicles, or on the shoulder ⟦17⟧. So a child cycling on the carriageway is a breach of the rules, but you must still be ready for it.
lesson.tip: The minimum age for cycling on the carriageway is 14; for a moped it is 16.

p: An e-scooter travels on a cycle track or cycle lane. If there is none, it travels at the right-hand edge of the carriageway (including in a lane for route vehicles) in single file, or on the shoulder ⟦18⟧.

From 25 August 2026, riding an e-scooter on pavements and footpaths is prohibited: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 326-VIII of 24.06.2026 removed this permission from the Road Traffic Act (art. 57(5)). The text of para. 168-1 still mentions the pavement (at a speed of up to 6 km/h), but the Act takes precedence, so the prohibition applies.

You may ride an e-scooter at the right-hand edge of the carriageway and in a lane for route vehicles only from the age of 18 and if you hold a driving licence of any category ⟦19⟧. On the carriageway, the helmet must be fastened ⟦20⟧.
list: Cycle track or cycle lane - first choice
No cycling infrastructure: right-hand edge of the carriageway (18+, licence, helmet) or the shoulder
Pavement and footpath - not allowed (from 25.08.2026). A cyclist without a cycle track may still use the pavement, if it does not impede pedestrians
From 1 July 2026, rental e-scooters must have registration plates and insurance
An e-scooter rider is fined for riding on the pavement as an “other road user” - 2 MCI (8 650 tenge), CAO art. 615

lesson.h: What is forbidden for cyclists and e-scooter riders
p: These prohibitions from para. 171 help a driver predict a cyclist's behaviour. For example, a cyclist must not turn left from a multi-lane road, so a sudden move to the left is a breach of the rules that you need to be ready for.
list: Riding without holding the handlebars with at least one hand
Carrying passengers (except on bicycles fitted with special equipment)
Carrying a load, except a load on bicycles fitted with special equipment and a load that projects no more than 50 cm
Turning left or making a U-turn on roads with tram traffic and on roads with more than one lane in that direction
Towing or being towed (except a bicycle trailer)
Crossing the carriageway on a pedestrian crossing while riding the vehicle: you must dismount
Riding on the carriageway during the hours of darkness without a retroreflective item
Riding on the carriageway without the helmet fastened

p: Riders of small electric vehicles (monowheels, hoverboards, segways and similar devices) are forbidden to ride on the carriageway, and to ride on the pavement or footpath if a cycle track or cycle lane is available nearby. They are also forbidden to ride without holding the handlebars (if there are any), to carry passengers or a load, to tow or be towed, or to cross the carriageway on a pedestrian crossing without getting off the device ⟦21⟧. Cycle tracks and cycle lanes are open to them: sign 4.5 permits bicycles, e-scooters and small electric vehicles.

You may ride a moped from the age of 16 ⟦22⟧. Mopeds must not use cycle tracks, cycle lanes, shoulders, pavements or footpaths (Road Traffic Act, art. 57(4)), and sign 4.5 does not permit mopeds. From 25 August 2026, bicycles with an engine are treated as mopeds (Law No. 326-VIII): they must be registered and insured, and riding one requires a category A1 driving licence (a category A or B licence also qualifies).

lesson.h: What this means for a car driver
p: On a cycle lane marked with sign 4.5 and plate 7.14, other vehicles must not drive or stop ⟦23⟧.

If this lane is separated from the rest of the carriageway by a broken line, you change lane into it before turning, giving way to cyclists riding along it ⟦24⟧. You may also move into it when entering the road, and to pick up or set down passengers at the right-hand edge ⟦25⟧.
When turning right or left, a driver gives way to cyclists who are using a cycle track to cross the road that the driver is turning into ⟦26⟧.

At an uncontrolled crossing of a cycle track with a road away from an intersection, the cyclist gives way to vehicles travelling on that road ⟦27⟧. But if the cyclist has already moved onto the road, your task is to avoid hitting them.
lesson.tip: A solid line next to a cycle lane - you must not move into it; a broken line - you may, to turn, to enter the road, or to pick up or set down passengers.

p: Convoys of cyclists on the carriageway are divided into groups of 10 cyclists (for carts, groups of 5). There is a gap of 80-100 m between groups, so that vehicles can overtake them easily ⟦28⟧.

Horse-drawn carts, riders and pack animals travel in the far right-hand lane in single file, or on the shoulder, if they do not impede pedestrians ⟦29⟧. When pulling out from a minor road at a place with poor visibility, the driver leads the animal by the bridle ⟦30⟧.

Animals are herded, as a rule, during daylight hours, close to the right-hand edge of the road ⟦31⟧. When crossing railway tracks, the herd is divided into groups ⟦32⟧. Animals must not be left unattended near paved roads, or herded outside places set aside for this ⟦33⟧.

If animals are herded in darkness, the herdsman warns drivers: standing 10-15 m from the herd, he swings a burning torch or a lantern by hand towards an approaching vehicle ⟦34⟧. If you see this signal, slow down.

Chapter 25 makes life easier for people who find it hard to walk. Signs 3.28, 3.29 and 3.30, which prohibit parking, do not apply to vehicles driven by drivers with a mobility disability, or to vehicles that serve such people or people with total loss of sight ⟦35⟧. Sign 3.27 does apply to them, but paras. 178-180 give special rights, described below. Such vehicles are fitted with suitable control mechanisms or adaptations.

Sign 5.15 with plate 7.17 “Persons with disabilities” marks a parking place only for invalid carriages and vehicles displaying the “Person with a disability” sign. Plate 7.18 “Except persons with disabilities” removes the effect of a prohibitory or mandatory sign for such vehicles ⟦36⟧.

A driver with a mobility disability, in a vehicle displaying the “Person with a disability” sign, may, in a built-up area, stop and leave the vehicle in the zone of signs prohibiting stopping or parking, if the vehicle stands entirely on the pavement and a strip at least 1.5 m wide is left for pedestrians. Where markings prohibit stopping, this does not apply ⟦37⟧. The same driver may also stay longer than the time limit in places with limited parking time, and in courtyards outside designated parking places, provided this does not obstruct anyone.

The driver of a vehicle with this sign that serves people with a mobility disability or total loss of sight may stop in the zone of signs prohibiting stopping, to pick up or set down such a person ⟦38⟧. If the driver walks the person by the hand to their destination and back, the vehicle is left on the conditions of para. 178: entirely on the pavement ⟦39⟧.

lesson.h: New Chapter 26: convoys in poor visibility
p: In fog, a blizzard or a dust storm, vehicles are sometimes driven in a convoy. Chapter 26 was added to the Rules in November 2025. Its point is that everyone drives as a single unit, behind the lead vehicle, and no one acts on their own.
list: A convoy travels in single file, as close as possible to the right-hand edge, unless it is escorted by emergency and special service vehicles ⟦40⟧
A convoy of more than 10 vehicles is escorted by at least 2 vehicles with a flashing blue, or blue and red, beacon ⟦41⟧
Speed and following distance are set by the convoy commander or the lead vehicle ⟦42⟧
A convoy without an escort is divided into groups of no more than 5 vehicles, with a distance between groups that allows overtaking ⟦43⟧
When a convoy stops on the road, everyone switches on their hazard warning lights ⟦44⟧
A member of the convoy follows the instructions of the lead vehicle and the rear vehicle, and keeps a safe following distance ⟦45⟧
You must not overtake other members of the convoy, leave the convoy, or stop without authorisation, except for a forced stop ⟦46⟧

lesson.h: How a convoy moves off and stops
p: Before moving off, everyone starts their engine and switches on dipped headlights or daytime running lights. Anyone who is not ready informs the rear vehicle. The rear vehicle blocks the lane, makes sure everything is safe, and gives permission to the lead vehicle. The lead vehicle sounds the horn and moves off ⟦47⟧.
To stop the convoy, the lead vehicle signals by braking and indicating right, reduces speed, pulls onto the shoulder and stops parallel to the road ⟦48⟧.
If you need to make an emergency stop, inform the lead vehicle by voice, by a hand signal, over the radio and (or) by flashing the main-beam headlights and sounding the horn ⟦49⟧.

When entering a parking area, a member of the convoy stops at the entrance and moves on once the vehicle ahead has finished parking ⟦50⟧. The convoy passes intersections, level crossings and traffic lights under the general rules. If a gap opens up, the rear vehicle informs the lead vehicle, who decides whether to stop or continue ⟦51⟧.

keyFacts: You may ride a moped from the age of 16 ⟦1⟧
Children under 14 must not ride a bicycle on the carriageway, in a lane for route vehicles, or on the shoulder ⟦2⟧
On the carriageway, an e-scooter may be ridden only from the age of 18, with a driving licence of any category and with the helmet fastened ⟦3⟧
From 25.08.2026, pavements and footpaths are prohibited for e-scooters (Law No. 326-VIII)
On a cycle lane (sign 4.5 with plate 7.14), other vehicles must not drive or stop ⟦4⟧
A load on a bicycle or e-scooter must not project more than 50 cm ⟦5⟧
Convoys of cyclists are divided into groups of 10, with 80-100 m between groups ⟦6⟧
At an uncontrolled crossing of a cycle track with a road away from an intersection, the cyclist gives way ⟦7⟧
A driver with a mobility disability, when leaving a vehicle on the pavement, must leave at least 1.5 m for pedestrians ⟦8⟧
A convoy of more than 10 vehicles is escorted by at least 2 vehicles with blue or blue-and-red beacons ⟦9⟧
A convoy without an escort is divided into groups of no more than 5 vehicles ⟦10⟧
When a convoy stops on the road, hazard warning lights are switched on in all vehicles ⟦11⟧
mistakes: Thinking you may ride an e-scooter on the pavement if you go no faster than 6 km/h. This rule has been repealed: from 25.08.2026, pavements and footpaths are closed to e-scooters (Law No. 326-VIII).

Thinking you may stop briefly on a cycle lane. You may not: other vehicles must not stop on a lane with sign 4.5 and plate 7.14. Moving into it is allowed only where the line is broken, and only to turn, to enter the road, or to pick up or set down passengers ⟦12⟧.
Thinking that a cyclist on a cycle track always has priority. At an uncontrolled crossing of a cycle track with a road away from an intersection, it is the cyclist who must give way ⟦13⟧.
Thinking a 12-year-old child may cycle at the edge of the road. On the carriageway and the shoulder, this is allowed only from the age of 14 ⟦14⟧.
Thinking you may overtake a slow neighbour in a convoy. Overtaking other members of the convoy is forbidden ⟦15⟧.
Thinking an e-scooter is just like a bicycle, so the pavement is allowed. A cyclist without a cycle track may use the pavement, but from 25.08.2026 e-scooters may not.
